label: rem:baryon-product-from-alt-proof-sketch
title: Proof sketch: baryon product from alt
html:
Proof sketch. By Schur–Weyl duality at level n = 3 in three dimensions (Schur–Weyl mass decomposition), the \mathrm{S}_3-module

  V \;:=\; \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3}\, T_{c_k}\mathbf{C}
  \;\cong\; R\,\langle dc_1/dz,\ dc_2/dz,\ dc_3/dz\rangle

decomposes into isotypic components labelled by partitions of 3:

  V \;\cong\; V_{(3)} \;\oplus\; V_{(1,1,1)} \;\oplus\; V_{(2,1)}
  \;=\; \mathrm{Sym}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Alt}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Std}^{\oplus 2}.

The dimensions are \dim_R V_{(3)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(1,1,1)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(2,1)} = 2, summing to 4. However, since V is the rank-3 permutation representation of \mathrm{S}_3, V \cong V_{(3)} \oplus V_{(2,1)}. The rank-1 alternating piece sits inside the exterior cube \Lambda^3 V. The relevant isotype is therefore the top exterior power.

By the Frobenius character formula (Frobenius universal) applied to \mathrm{S}_3, the projector onto the sign isotype of any \mathrm{S}_3-module W is

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_3|} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\, \sigma
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6}\bigl(
    \mathrm{id} - (12) - (13) - (23) + (123) + (132)
  \bigr).

Applied to dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz \in V^{\otimes 3}, this projector yields the antisymmetrisation

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}\bigl(dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\,
    \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3} dc_{\sigma(k)}/dz.

Write v_k := dc_k/dz. Under the canonical isomorphism \Lambda^3 V \cong R, the antisymmetrised tensor maps to v_1 \wedge v_2 \wedge v_3. On the diagonal frame \bigl(v_k\, e_k\bigr)_{k=1}^{3} this is \bigl(\prod_k v_k\bigr)\, e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3. The sign change under sheet exchange is carried by e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3, not by the coefficient: after the identification e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3 \mapsto 1, which is not \mathrm{S}_3-equivariant, the scalar \prod_k v_k is symmetric. So the product is not a sign-isotypic scalar.

The sign-isotypic scalars are the antisymmetric polynomials in v_1, v_2, v_3. Applying \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}} to the monomial v_1^0 v_2^1 v_3^2 gives \tfrac{1}{6}\sum_{\sigma} \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\, v_{\sigma(2)}\, v_{\sigma(3)}^2, which is \tfrac{1}{6} times the 3 \times 3 Vandermonde determinant. Its cofactor expansion factors as

  (v_2 v_3^2 - v_3 v_2^2) - v_1 (v_3^2 - v_2^2) + v_1^2 (v_3 - v_2)
  \;=\;
  (v_2 - v_1)(v_3 - v_1)(v_3 - v_2)
  \;=\; \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}},

an identity in any commutative ring. Every antisymmetric polynomial is divisible by each v_j - v_i, hence by \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}, with symmetric quotient; so \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} spans the lowest-degree part of the sign isotype.

R-rationality. By implicit differentiation v_k = -(\partial F/\partial z)/(\partial F/\partial c) at (z, c_k), a rational function of c_k over R(z). The ratio \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} / V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3) is symmetric in the roots, hence lies in R(z), and the squared Vandermonde of the roots is the discriminant of the cubic (color-tube cubic):

  V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)^2
  \;=\;
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} (c_i - c_j)^2
  \;=\;
  \Delta(z)
  \;\in\; R[z].

So \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}^2 \in R(z), and \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} itself lies in R(z)\bigl(\sqrt{\Delta(z)}\bigr). \square

The sum \sum_k dc_k/dz spans the degree-one part of the trivial isotype V_{(3)}, the integrand for a symmetric trion. The baryon sits in the antisymmetric colour singlet \mathrm{Alt}^3, selecting the velocity Vandermonde. This algebraic selection requires no input from the Picard–Lefschetz machinery. Both the Vandermonde and \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}} are defined over R; the baryon integrand evaluation remains R-rational until the archimedean fibre functor \tau is applied.

This algebraic choice of the sign block, combined with the scalar weight w_\lambda from the Markov trace (categorical mass as Markov trace), fully determines the baryon integrand \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}.

Scope of the selection — derived versus input. Two claims must be kept apart. That \mathrm{Alt}^3 is a genuinely non-trivial one-dimensional representation is derived: the monodromy of the color-tube cubic F around its discriminant is the full \mathrm{S}_3, computed exactly over R = \mathbb{Q}[z] (irreducibility over \mathbb{C}(z) gives transitivity; the depressed quadratic is coprime to \Delta, so every one of the six simple branch points carries a transposition, and a transitive subgroup of \mathrm{S}_3 with a transposition is \mathrm{S}_3) and confirmed at 50 digits by transporting the three sheets around all six branch points — every loop returns a transposition and the six generate \mathrm{S}_3 (monodromy witness). Had the group been only A_3, the sign line would coincide with the trivial one and selecting \mathrm{Alt}^3 would carry no information; the surjectivity onto \{\pm 1\} rules that out. What remains an input — not derived from the categorical substrate — is that the physical baryon occupies \mathrm{Alt}^3 rather than the trivial or standard isotype: this is the color-singlet (confinement) condition. Stating the occupation as a derivation would conflate an invariant of the fibre (the non-trivial sign line, which the geometry supplies) with the channel of the state (which it does not), and is the standing open item.
